title: QBI Deduction 2026: Eligibility, Income Limits, and Examples
summary: Understand the QBI deduction in 2026, who qualifies, income thresholds, the new minimum deduction, and how year-end business purchases can affect your tax bill.
body_markdown:
*Illustrative financial-planning photo by* *[Kelly Sikkema on Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/person-reviewing-documents-with-calculator-and-laptop-0oZpRxG5Hkk)* *.*


The **QBI deduction** can reduce the federal taxable income of qualifying business owners. The 2025 tax law made it permanent, removing the scheduled expiration after 2025. For 2026, it also introduced a minimum deduction for certain active business owners and widened the income range over which additional restrictions take effect.[Section 199A](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t26/s199A/)


The familiar 20% figure is still part of the calculation. But claiming it starts with three questions: how is your business taxed, what income qualifies, and what is your taxable income on the owner’s return?


## What Is the Qualified Business Income Deduction?


The **qualified business income deduction** , also called the **Section 199A deduction** , generally allows eligible owners to deduct up to 20% of qualifying net business income, subject to limits. It can be claimed whether you take the standard deduction or itemize.[IRS overview](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/qualified-business-income-deduction)


It reduces taxable income. The actual tax saving depends on the owner’s tax situation. A $20,000 deduction does not mean a $20,000 refund or a 20% reduction in the business’s entire tax bill.


### What Does “Permanent” Mean?


The law no longer contains the previous end-of-2025 sunset. Owners still need to qualify and calculate the deduction each year. Annual inflation adjustments and changes in income can produce a different result even when the business itself stays much the same.


## Who Qualifies for the QBI Deduction?


Owners of sole proprietorships, partnerships, and S corporations may qualify, along with some trusts and estates. For partnerships and S corporations, the deduction is determined at the partner or shareholder level. The business supplies information that the owner uses on their return.[IRS eligibility guidance](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/qualified-business-income-deduction)


### Does an LLC Qualify?


An LLC’s federal tax treatment matters. An LLC taxed as a sole proprietorship, partnership, or S corporation may generate qualifying income. An LLC taxed as a C corporation does not generate an owner-level **QBI deduction** from that corporation’s earnings.[IRS LLC classifications](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/limited-liability-company-llc)


### Which Income Is Excluded?


Employee wages and income earned through a C corporation are excluded. An S corporation owner’s reasonable compensation and a partner’s guaranteed payments for services are also excluded from that recipient’s QBI. Capital gains and many investment-income items have separate treatment.[Section 199A income rules](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t26/s199A/)


## What Counts as Qualified Business Income?


QBI starts with qualifying business income after related deductions and losses. Gross sales alone cannot tell you the deduction. An importer with substantial revenue may have a much smaller qualifying profit after inventory costs, wages, freight, rent, and other deductible expenses.


Deductions attributable to the business, including qualifying retirement contributions, self-employed health insurance, and the deductible portion of self-employment tax, can also affect QBI. Loss carryforwards need attention.[IRS calculation guidance](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8995)


For a US importer, buying goods overseas does not by itself make the resulting business profit foreign income. The relevant rule concerns income effectively connected with conducting a US trade or business. Cross-border activities can require a closer review.


## By the Numbers: What Changed for 2026?


20%: the basic QBI percentage, before applicable limitations.


$400: the new minimum deduction for qualifying active business owners.


$1,000: the minimum aggregate QBI from active qualified businesses needed for that $400 floor.


These amounts come from[Section 199A](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t26/s199A/) . An active qualified business is one in which the taxpayer materially participates under the tax rules. The $400 floor replaces a smaller calculated deduction for an eligible taxpayer; it is not an extra $400 added to every deduction. The minimum and eligibility amount become inflation-adjusted after 2026.


## What Are the QBI Income Limits for 2026?


The **QBI income limits** use taxable income calculated before the **QBI deduction** , under the Section 199A rules. They are measured on the taxpayer’s return. A spouse’s income on a joint return can therefore affect the result.


Figure 1 shows the[IRS thresholds for tax years beginning in 2026](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf) . The two ends of each range mark when additional restrictions begin and become fully effective.


*Figure 1.* ***QBI deduction*** *thresholds and restriction ranges for 2026. Sources:* *[IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, section 4.26](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf)* *and* *[Section 199A](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t26/s199A/)* *.*


### Below the Threshold


At or below the applicable threshold, the W-2 wage and qualified-property limitation does not apply, and specified service businesses can qualify. The normal overall taxable-income cap still matters, subject to the new minimum deduction for qualifying active owners.


### Within or Above the Range


Above the threshold, restrictions phase in. For a business that is not a specified service trade or business, the deduction may be limited by wages and qualifying depreciable property. Passing the upper figure does not automatically eliminate every business owner’s deduction.[Statutory limitation rules](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t26/s199A/)


### What Is a Specified Service Trade or Business?


This category, commonly shortened to SSTB, includes fields such as health, law, accounting, and consulting. Its qualifying income is progressively restricted through the applicable range and excluded at or above the upper endpoint. A business with mixed activities needs a classification review.[IRS SSTB guidance](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8995a)


Payroll, property records, and the owner’s wider income picture become especially useful when a business approaches these thresholds. Keep the supporting records alongside the year-end forecast.

## A Simple QBI Deduction Example


Assume a single owner has $100,000 of QBI and $140,000 of taxable income before the deduction, calculated under the applicable rules. Assume no net capital gain, qualified dividends, REIT or publicly traded partnership income, prior QBI losses, or cooperative adjustments.


The basic QBI amount is $20,000. The ordinary taxable-income cap is $28,000, so the smaller amount gives a $20,000 deduction. This illustrative owner is below the 2026 threshold, so wage and property restrictions do not apply.[IRS calculation framework](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/qualified-business-income-deduction)


The deduction’s tax value depends on the owner’s tax rates and other circumstances. Net capital gain, including qualified dividends for this calculation, can reduce the overall taxable-income cap.


## How Year-End Purchases Can Affect QBI


An equipment deduction can lower business income and also reduce the income used for the QBI calculation. For an owner receiving an unrestricted 20% **QBI deduction** , an additional $10,000 deductible business expense could reduce the **QBI deduction** by $2,000. In that simplified case, taxable income falls by $8,000 overall. This illustration assumes all other limits and adjustments remain unchanged.


Ask your accountant to compare the combined result before accelerating a purchase. ## How Do You Claim the Deduction?


Use[Form 8995](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8995) or Form 8995-A, as applicable, with your tax return. Use the form and instructions for the tax year you are filing. Partnerships and S corporations provide relevant information through Schedule K-1 and supporting statements.


Collect the records in Figure 2 before the year-end discussion. If your business has losses, multiple activities, cooperative income, or changing ownership, flag those details for your preparer.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is the QBI Deduction Permanent?


Yes. The 2025 law removed the scheduled expiration after 2025. Eligibility and annual calculation rules still apply.


### Can I Claim QBI With the Standard Deduction?


Yes, qualifying taxpayers can claim it with either the standard deduction or itemized deductions. The amount remains subject to the applicable QBI rules.


### Does the Deduction Reduce Self-Employment Tax?


The **QBI deduction** itself does not reduce self-employment tax. It is an income-tax deduction, so include self-employment tax separately in your estimate.


### Does Every Business Owner Get the New $400 Minimum?


No. For 2026, the owner needs at least $1,000 of aggregate QBI from active qualified businesses in which they materially participate. An eligible owner receives the greater of the regular deduction and $400.
